text:
Ryan Leonard was on the ice for the moment that won Washington's game today: he set up Aliaksei Protas's go-ahead goal on a new line with Pierre-Luc Dubois, on a night the Capitals had to play most of the game without Tom Wilson. It fits his season. He has 11 points in 15 games in just over 14 minutes a night, and he scores at a rate per 60 minutes well above a typical forward.

What stands out is the shooting. He has 39 shots, his own chances are up to 1.24 expected goals per 60 from 0.87 last season, and his top shot speed is in the 97th percentile in the league. Five goals on about four and a third expected is barely hot, so this scoring is built to last. The 5v5 share with him on is about even (52%), and Evolving-Hockey flagged the defensive cost last season (bottom 9% of forwards at limiting chances), offset by drawing more penalties than he takes. Our projection has him around 24 goals and 52 points. The question for the next few weeks is whether the Dubois line sticks and brings more minutes with it.
headline: Ryan Leonard gets a new center and keeps shooting
